specs.cpu: Intel Core 3 N355 (8-core: 8 E-cores (Alder Lake-N, no P-cores), Alder Lake-N refresh, up to 3.9 GHz)

battery.notes: Same low-power N355 + ChromeOS recipe as the Lenovo: ~8-10h real web use.

ASUS Chromebook Plus CX14, 14" 16:9 FHD (1920 x 1080) Anti-Glare Touchscreen Display, Intel Core 3-N355 Processor, 256GB Storage, 8GB RAM, Wi-Fi 6, ChromeOS, Rock Grey, CX1405CTA-AS31T-CB

reviews.quote: A bargain laptop that's actually fast - the Core 3 processor ensures the system feels fast and stable at all times, with a clear performance leap over simple Chromebooks.
ChromeOS charm on a shoestring: a decent performer with attractive price, but it's not the best-built laptop, with an all-plastic construction that isn't very rigid.

praises: $599.99 sale gets touchscreen + 256GB storage on the new N355 — the touch pick of the value tier
Same near-silent, cool-running N355 platform as the best-value Lenovo
Chromebook Plus minimums met: 8GB RAM, 1080p webcam, ~10-year update window
Touchscreen is genuinely useful on ChromeOS for scrolling and Android apps
ASUS's CX-series chassis feels sturdier than the no-name sub-$400 Chromebooks
complaints: eMMC storage (not SSD) — slower than the Lenovo's SSD at $150 less, and soldered
$749.99 regular price is poor value; only the $599.99 sale is honest
Glossy touch panel is reflective and class-typical washed colour
No active pen support despite the touch layer
N355 is fine for web but the $699.97 CX34 i5 twin is a much faster machine

standouts: Cheapest touchscreen Chromebook Plus in the CA inventory at $599.99 sale
design_philosophy: The CX14 is ASUS's refresh of the value Chromebook Plus: current-gen N355 efficiency, a touchscreen as the differentiator, and 256GB to ease the soldered-storage problem — while keeping costs down with eMMC and a plastic chassis. It slots between the $450 Lenovo and the $700 CX34 as the 'touch on a budget' option.
